qualitative.gate_2_reason: Accessible-luxury fashion handbags and leather accessories are deferrable discretionary purchases exposed to fashion-trend cyclicality and middle-class spending pullbacks, not essential needs, everyday staple rituals, or ultra-affluent Lindy scarcity luxury.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Essential Western Need, REJECT). While Coach is enjoying a strong FY25-FY26 brand resurgence (77.8% consolidated gross margin, $8.00B FY26 revenue), Tapestry's accessible-luxury handbags and accessories remain non-essential, easily deferred discretionary fashion goods rather than functional necessities, daily habits, or Lindy ultra-luxury scarcity franchises like Hermes or Ferrari. Multi-cycle cyclicality and brand-trend fragility are evidenced by TPR's -22.8% FY20 revenue drop, six-year FY18-FY24 top-line stagnation ($5.98B to $6.77B), the August 2025 divestiture of Stuart Weitzman, and Kate Spade's ongoing ~10% revenue contraction and operating losses. Also note empire-building M&A risk demonstrated by the attempted $8.5B Capri deal (halted only by FTC antitrust injunction in Nov 2024).
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle track record shows fashion-cycle sensitivity masked by Coach's recent surge: revenue moved from ~$5.98B (FY18) to ~$4.64B (FY20, -22.8%, gross margin ~65.3%) and stalled between $6.51B and $6.77B over FY21-FY24 before reaching $7.01B in FY25 ($1.39B GAAP operating income, ~$1.1B FCF, 75.4% gross margin) and $8.00B in FY26 (+14.2% YoY, $1.86B GAAP operating income, ~$1.8B-$1.9B FCF, 77.8% gross margin). 10-year historical ROIC averaged 15.2% (baseline financials) before rising above 36% in FY26 alongside buybacks. Brand mix is heavily skewed: Coach (~88% of revenue) grew 24% in FY26 at ~35.5% operating margins via Gen-Z traction and lower promotions, whereas Kate Spade declined ~10% with operating losses during a multi-year reset, and Stuart Weitzman was divested in August 2025. Capital allocation shifted to a $2B+ buyback program and ~1.1x gross debt/adjusted EBITDA ($1.1B+ cash) only after a federal court blocked Tapestry's debt-funded $8.5B Capri Holdings acquisition in late 2024.
